Individual first frequencies and simultaneous highest frequencies give the two spectral endpoint bounds, and nonnegative holding gives the weight budget. Minimizing the two-line bound yields t*=min(1/(2S),2/(1+R)); the proposed direction-invariant kernel attains it by its full Fourier spectrum. Equality forces the stated direction-invariant rates via the active negative endpoint or saturated budget. The odd half-angle contribution is strictly above 1/4 and at most 1/3, with equality at 3, yielding exactly the stated criterion including its boundary. For the common-weight restriction the optimal weight is between 2/(4d+delta_1) and 1/(2d) for large N, giving the O(N^-4) remainder in its gap and the ratio d. No unrestricted uniqueness is needed or claimed.
